lesson.title: Pulled Wide? Buy Time First
lesson.hook: You get dragged off the court and try to hit your way out, while the court you left stays empty.
lesson.tomorrow: Next time you're pulled off the court, hit high and deep and use the flight time to get back.

pro.label: Defence isn't lost
pro.moment: Once they're on defence, ATP players still win 31% of points. Alcaraz is the best at it, at 38%.
pro.read: Buy the time and you're still in the point.

drill.name: Buy time
drill.how: Your partner pulls you wide with a feed. Your reply must clear the net by a racquet's length and land past the service line. Then play the point out.

steps.name: Pulled wide, low and late
steps.sit: Their angle pulls you off the court. You reach it low and late; they're in the middle.
steps.q: What do you do with it?
opts: Flat and deep down the line
steps.payoff: Height and depth give you time to get back to the middle.
steps.principle: When you're off the court, the next job is getting back, not winning the point.
steps.why: From low and wide, a flat ball comes back before you've recovered. A high, deep ball takes longer to cross and they can't attack it, so you're back in position.
steps.take: Pulled wide? Go high and deep, and use the time to get back.

lines.A: Low, late and flat at the line — it sails long.
lines.B: Hard and flat, it's back quickly — you're still stretched.
lines.C: High and deep: the flight time gets you back — you're in time.
lines.D: Short — they step in and it's past you.

steps.name: Early, and they're stuck
steps.sit: This one isn't as wide. You're there early, and they're still in their forehand corner.
steps.q: What does this ball let you do?
steps.payoff: Early and balanced, with them stuck in the corner: now the open court is yours.
steps.principle: Buy time when you're late. Attack when you're early.
steps.why: The high ball was the answer when you were late. Here you have time, and they haven't moved from the corner, so the open court is too far for them. The line is a winner 7 times in 10; the high crosscourt lands every time and leaves you set early, so both are good choices.
steps.take: Early, and they're stuck in a corner? Hit into the open court.

lines.A: They're stuck in the corner — too far to get across. Winner.
lines.B: Back to where they're standing — you're only just in time.
lines.C: Also fine: it lands every time and you're set early. The line wins, 7 in 10.
lines.D: Through the middle — they get it back; you're only just in time.

steps.name: Pulled wide on the backhand
steps.sit: Now the angle pulls you off the court on your backhand side. Low and late again.
opts: Flat and deep down the line
steps.payoff: Same problem, other wing: height and depth buy the time.
steps.principle: The wing doesn't change the job: get back first.
steps.why: From low and wide on the backhand, the flat ball and the short slice both leave you stranded. High and deep crosscourt gives you net, court and time.
steps.take: Low and wide, either wing? High and deep crosscourt, then recover.

lines.A: Hard and flat, it's back before you are — too far to get there.
lines.B: Short — they step in and it's past you.
lines.C: Low, late and flat at the line — it sails long.
lines.D: High and deep buys the time to get back — you're in time.
